security_frame.attacker: Software holding write access to the CSRNG register block, at the privilege level able to program INT_STATE_READ_ENABLE and CTRL.READ_INT_STATE. The parties affected are the other CSRNG applications, including the hardware EDN instances whose DRBG state that software is not authorized to see.
security_frame.precondition: The CSRNG is enabled, at least two applications have been instantiated so their internal states hold distinct key material, and the internal-state read path is open (CTRL.READ_INT_STATE set, otp_en_csrng_sw_app_read enabling, INT_STATE_READ_ENABLE_REGWEN still permitting writes to the enable mask).
security_frame.input: Program INT_STATE_READ_ENABLE with bit 0 set and the target application's bit clear, then select the target application through INT_STATE_READ_ID and read INT_STATE_VAL repeatedly to walk the 32-bit dump window.
security_frame.protected_asset: The internal DRBG state of each CSRNG application: the AES key and the V counter block, from which that application's future random output can be predicted.
security_frame.security_property: src/csrng/data/csrng.rdl:220-228 describes INT_STATE_READ_ENABLE as a per-instance enable and states that each bit defines whether the internal state of the corresponding instance is readable, and src/csrng/data/csrng.hjson:306 states that the bit of the selected instance must be set for a read to work. So the dump of application N must be permitted exactly when bit N is set.
security_frame.implemented_logic: src/csrng/rtl/csrng_state_db.sv:115 forms the dump qualification as int_st_dump_sel & {NApps{int_state_read_enable_i[0]}}, replicating bit 0 across every application lane. The assignment sits outside the per-application generate loop that opens on the next line, so it has no index available; the two sibling selects inside that loop are both indexed by rd. Application 0's authorization bit therefore decides whether any application's internal state may be dumped, in both directions.

security_feature_bypassed: Per-application authorization of CSRNG internal-state reads (INT_STATE_READ_ENABLE), the control that keeps one application's DRBG key and V from being read out through another application's authorization.
proof_goal: Establish that the dump window serves an application whose own authorization bit is clear, and withholds an application whose own bit is set, so that bit 0 is the effective gate for all applications; and that the exposed word is key material rather than the separately-exported reseed counter.
proof_style: Directed port-driven simulation of one real csrng_state_db, paired with a scripted structural audit of the submitted tree and a negative control that indexes the qualification per application.
invariant: A read of application N's internal state through the register dump window must return that application's state when int_state_read_enable_i[N] is set, and must return zero when int_state_read_enable_i[N] is clear, independent of the value of any other bit of the vector.
attacker_model: Privileged software at supervisor mode, being the level that programs the CSRNG enable mask and the internal-state read controls. No physical access and no debug access is needed.
minimum_attack_sequence: Ensure two applications hold distinct internal state (each has been instantiated).
Write INT_STATE_READ_ENABLE so that bit 0 is set and the target application's own bit is clear.
Write INT_STATE_READ_ID with the target application's id, which latches the dump target and rewinds the read pointer.
Read INT_STATE_VAL repeatedly to advance the pointer into the key field and collect the target application's DRBG key words.
controls: control_app0_authorized_reads_app0: application 0 authorized by its own bit must be readable, showing the harness can produce a successful key dump at all.
violating_app1_denied_but_readable: with only bit 0 set, application 1's key must dump as zeros. This is the over-privileged read.

violating_app1_authorized_but_denied: with only bit 1 set, application 1's key must be served. This is the mirror case, and it is what proves bit 0 is the effective gate rather than merely an additional condition.
containment_all_bits_clear_denies_all: with the whole vector clear no application may be dumped, separating a mis-indexed gate from an absent one.
witness_construction_note: Every probe reads a word of the DRBG key, not word 0 of the window. src/csrng/rtl/csrng_state_db.sv:180 exports the reseed counter unconditionally through reseed_counter_o, and the tree documents the counter as always readable, so a counter word would be a weak witness. The concatenation at :135-137 orders the state as {fips, inst_st, key, v, res_ctr}, placing the key at window words 5 through 12. Each application is loaded with a distinct marker key so any word read back identifies which application it came from. The harness drives only declared ports: states are loaded through the write handshake and read through the status interface, exactly as csrng_core drives them. There is no force, no deposit and no hierarchical assignment.
expected_evidence: A key word belonging to application 1 read out of the window while INT_STATE_READ_ENABLE leaves bit 1 clear.
Zero read out for application 1 while bit 1 is set, in the same run.
Both violations disappearing once the qualification is indexed per application.
success_criteria: checks=4 and fails=2 in the directed simulation, the two failures being the two violating cases.
The negative control fails the identical testbench once the qualification is indexed, reporting both violating cases as PASS and no witness lines.
non_findings: No claim that the reseed counter is improperly exposed: the tree exports it unconditionally by design.
No claim about the hardware read path (state_db_rd_* ), which is correctly indexed at :118 and is not software-visible.
No claim that the outer gates (CTRL.READ_INT_STATE, otp_en_csrng_sw_app_read, the regwen) are themselves bypassed; the defect is inside the per-application layer beneath them.
